children: , the global banking and wealth-management group, raised its year-end S&P 500 target to 8,100 from 7,650. The upgraded forecast leaves roughly 4.9% upside from the index's previous close. HSBC's U.S. shares edged lower to $107.08.

The 450-point upgrade lifts HSBC's target by 5.9%. The bank expects S&P 500 earnings per share to surge more than 25% during the second half after 86% of reporting companies beat quarterly estimateswell above the historical rate of approximately 67.5%. The message is simple: profits are doing the heavy lifting, and HSBC believes the earnings engine still has fuel.

HSBC's first-half results reinforce that bullish stance, with revenue rising 11% to $37.7 billion and reported pretax profit jumping 23% to $19.5 billion. Yet the valuation picture demands caution: HSBC shares trade 68.47% above their GF Value estimate of $63.56. With the S&P 500 already up 12.75% this year and HSBC carrying a sizable valuation premium, earnings must now deliverthe market has left little room for disappointment.

title: HSBC's 8,100 S&P Target Needs a 25% Earnings Sprint
